title: War as Peace
subtitle: Seeing social force as Einstein saw physical force

blocks.html: Standing still, we used to feel the forces of our bodies and the Earth oppose each other. Falling was acceleration. When we threw rocks and when we fired cannonballs, they did not fly straight—they curved toward the ground.

Today, we are aware (on some level) that our intuitive picture is only a convenience. Inside the close-up concept, falling is stillness; standing is accelerating upward; projectiles do fly straight; and, while they fly, space flows (from our “timelike” point of view).
The single most important question in human political, economic, and psychological theory has been whether to seek the end of war. Is war a permanent feature of human life?
